DoorDash is looking for an Engineering Manager with an ML background to lead the Personalization engineering team. This team is responsible for building ML ranking and recommendation systems to maximize the value for consumers, merchants, and DoorDash.
Our Personalization team is a part of our Core Consumer org which owns the top of the conversion funnel from the initial landing page all the way to checkout across platforms. Personalization is at the center of the team’s mission. As DoorDash expands into new verticals and experiences like grocery, reservations, and going out, the challenge of helping consumers easily find what they want grows exponentially, so the opportunity is massive!
In 2027, we’re reimagining personalization from the ground up: an intent agent that predicts, at app open, what each consumer is here for; semantic understanding of every entity we rank; a blender that blends content from different verticals and business lines, like reservations, going out, and ads; and real-time ranking that adapts as consumer signals happen.

You will lead a team of world-class ML engineers redefining the personalization experience for DoorDash through cutting-edge technologies. You will also be the key player in defining DoorDash’s personalization strategy and technology roadmap.

Build an intent agent that makes granular predictions of what each consumer is here for the moment they open the app, and shapes the experience around it
Leverage cutting-edge LLM and Deep Learning (GNN, MTL, Transformers) to augment DoorDash’s personalization stack, starting with semantic understanding of every entity we rank, so our models understand what consumers want and what we offer, not just what they clicked before
Extend the blender to blend content from different verticals and business lines, like reservations, going out, and ads, balancing value for consumers, merchants, and DoorDash
Take personalization to real-time ranking that reacts to consumer signals as they happen

Work with Product, Design, and Business stakeholders directly across DoorDash to define the roadmap and vision for the team and deliver immense impact

We're excited about you because you have…
B.S., M.S., or PhD. in Computer Science or equivalent
7+ years of industry experience
Minimum of 2 years of leadership experience
Broad knowledge of machine learning with strong ML modeling foundation
Extensive experience in building user-facing product and working directly with product managers

The primary focus of this role is to lead DoorDash’s efforts to maintain optimal work environments that foster positive relationships and two-way communication between employees and leadership. Reporting to the Senior Manager, People Advocacy, the role will help serve as a critical resource to a wide variety of cross-functional teams who support DoorDash’s New Verticals and Customer Service teams.
About the Role
As the Manager, People Advocacy, you will partner with a team responsible for identifying and addressing issues impacting the employee experience of our customer-facing teammates.  You will also partner closely with business leaders, Employment Legal, HR Business Partners, Employee Relations, and other functions within the People Team to address identified opportunities.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Design, develop and execute both the strategic and tactical components of DoorDash’s employee advocacy strategy.
Work with partners across the organization to drive positive employee relations.
Develop, deploy and leverage communication channels to obtain employee feedback and implement action plans focused on addressing identified opportunities.
Create and implement training focused on improving overall people leadership skills.
Monitor Employee Relations trends, local and federal law changes, and rulings that have potential impact to DoorDash.
Inform leadership and people teams about the potential impacts on employee experience resulting from new initiatives, policies, and programs.
What You Will Own
Case and Project Management
Research and responses to employee relations matters both virtually and in person.  Assist HR Business Partners and ER Business Partners in resolving concerns.
Guidance to leaders to appropriately resolve concerns and mitigate employment risk.
Employee Advocacy, Training, Communication
Influence business decisions to balance employee and business impact.
Train leadership on topics related to creating an optimal working relationship with employees.
Assess working conditions, safety, employee experience and leadership effectiveness.
Conduct on-site response to engagement and environmental concerns.
Deliver site-specific action plans and follow up.
Analytics

description:

DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike.  We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact.  We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries.  As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries.  We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better

location: New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Los Angeles, CA; Chicago, IL; Austin, TX; Denver, CO; Seattle, WA; Miami, FL
description:
About the team
The Digital Ordering team is DoorDash’s hyper-growth business segment that aims to revolutionize the “first-party” digital experiences for Merchants and their Customers. We are helping Restaurants grow their same store sales through all of their owned channels. We do that by building custom Apps and Websites that offer best in class performance. Our team’s mission is to enhance our Merchants’ digital experiences and, in doing so, drive exponential growth for the Platform business.
Said differently, we are looking for top technical talent to help us drive exponential growth for our hypergrowth SaaS business.
About the role
As a Senior Manager, Product Ops on the DoorDash Digital Ordering team, you will play a critical role in driving growth across our various products and services. You will report into the General Manager for the Digital Ordering and Point of Sale within DoorDash’s broader DashOS org.
You will have to key priorities:
To utilize your growth sense and technical expertise (commerce experience strongly preferred) to guide merchants through how the DoorDash Commerce Platform can fit into their business, team and tech infrastructure.  You’ll do this by becoming an expert in both our product suite as well as restaurant tech stacks, processes, and common challenges.  You will play a mix of a role as both a consultant and key contributor to the sales process. Your key Merchant points of contact will be CEOs, CTOs, and CMOs
Lead a team whose primary objectives are to influence our product road map and drive same store sales (i.e. growth) for our Merchants via Quality initiatives & Growth experimentation.  Our products are designed to help restaurants exponentially alter their growth trajectory and you will work alongside them to iteratively optimize their same store sales through experimentation, analysis, marketing, and more.
Join to help us:
Scale a business that is a pivotal strategic bet for the company
Build an AI forward set of Commerce tools
Help merchants customize and optimize their first-party digital ordering experience
Work on high-visibility initiatives alongside cross-functional leaders in product, engineering, and strategy
Leverage a data-driven approach to guide optimizing both your time and merchant resources
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Leverage your technical (commerce expertise) to Consult & Win new Business: Build trust with merchants and help guide them through complex decisions to re-envision their tech stack to unlock greater same store sales growth for their first party channels.
Produce differentiated growth: Drive measurable results by focusing resources on the areas of greatest opportunity, adding value through the breadth of experience you bring to the table.
Operate: Dive into the lowest level of detail to ensure successful execution. You will meticulously anticipate and address potential challenges as we rapidly scale. You will work directly with internal and external partners to implement strategies and scale processes while maintaining operational excellence.
Strategize: Develop comprehensive strategies to support and scale the Digital Ordering business, considering both immediate and long-term success. You will tailor strategies to leverage DoorDash’s technology and maximize impact & growth for our Restaurant partners.
Build & own: Establish and own the infrastructure needed for massive growth in the business. From there, you will lead 0 to 1 opportunities, creating roadmaps for future growth vectors and owning key outcomes.
Collaborate: Value and build strong partnerships with our merchant partners and across DoorDash, including Product, Engineering, Account Management, Analytics, Finance, and many others. You will work together to bring your strategies to life.
Analyze: Leverage complex datasets and qualitative inputs to generate insights and recommendations. You will use data and experimentation to refine processes and drive measurable improvements for internal and external stakeholders.
Communicate & advocate: Represent the DoorDash brand with humility and a customer-first mindset. You will navigate ambiguous environments and provide structure for undefined opportunities by creating playbooks and templates. You will precisely communicate your plans to align your team and cross-functional partners with your goals.
We’re excited about you because…
You have relevant experience. You have 8-10+ years of experience in solutions architecture (commerce experience strongly preferred), sales engineering, growth, product, product ops, strategy/biz ops, or technical GTM roles – ideally in a fast-paced environment focused on outcomes.
You’re a strong communicator: you can interface with senior audiences, internally and externally; you can easily articulate complex details and help audiences quickly understand the “so what”.
You’ve been told you have a high EQ: you know how to “read the room” and can quickly build rapport + credibility with XFN partners (esp technical and senior audiences).
You have a strong growth sense: you know the difference between signal and noise, how to pull levers to iteratively optimize within a feedback loop.
You have an extreme sense of ownership: you take full responsibility for your scope of work. You are proactive in solving ambiguous problems and inspire your teammates to excel.
You’re detail-oriented: you have meticulous attention to detail, ensuring no small element is overlooked. Your thoroughness helps you anticipate issues and plan beyond immediate tasks.
You’re a builder: you thrive on building from the ground up. You excel at creating structure and process, and you’re resourceful in figuring out answers to complex questions with minimal oversight.  You’ve used many software tools and are ready to dive into learning how to leverage new ones.
You’re low ego: you want to GSD and are willing to do whatever it takes to make that happen; no responsibility or task is too trivial or “too tactical.”
You move fast: speed excites you. You prefer to achieve results today rather than waiting for tomorrow.
You can toggle between strategic and tactical: you’re equally comfortable with thinking through complex problems and getting into the weeds to execute.
You are an eager learner: ecomm, tech and digital spaces are rapidly evolving, but you enjoy learning how to incorporate new technologies into your approach and are ready to self-teach by diving into technical documentation.

We are leaders: Leadership is not limited to our management team. Everyone at DoorDash embraces and embodies leadership.
We are doers: We believe the only way to predict the future is to build it. Creating solutions that lead our company and industry is what we do.

title: Senior Manager, Protective Services
description:
About the Team
DoorDash is one of the world's most trusted on-demand logistics platforms. The Global Safety and Security team exists to keep it that way, protecting our people, property, operations, brand, and reputation across all our markets. We manage risk and create value through agility, technology, and a people-first approach. Our DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt brands now span more than 40 countries, dozens of offices, and tens of thousands of employees. Protective Services is the function accountable for the safety of the people we protect and the environments they live and work in, wherever they are.
About the Role
We are hiring a Senior Manager, Protective Services to lead protective operations, reporting to the Director, Protective Services. This is as much a build-and-execute mandate as a leadership one. You own the decisions that keep protection working, including how teams are staffed and assigned, how protection is set for a given person and situation, what we spend and which vendors we use, what people are trained to do, and how incidents get handled.
This is a player-coach role, and the coaching half does not keep you off the field. You will work advances, travel with the people we protect, and take your turn in the rotation while setting the standard the team works to. Protection here is a service. It works when the people we protect can move through their lives with as little friction as we can manage, and when they trust the team enough to tell us what we need to know.
You own protective operations, training and standards, vendor management, incident response, and converged physical-cyber protection. Protective teams, intelligence, and cybersecurity work on the same problem simultaneously, and detection and intelligence capabilities drive our protective posture.
Success in the first year means a tight operating rhythm, training and qualification standards that hold up against the best protective programs, a team that is current and deployable on short notice, and protective decisions driven by intelligence rather than reaction.
You are excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead protective operations. Own staffing, assignment, protective decisions, resourcing, and response across the full scope of the program. Lead from within the work rather than from above it, and be accountable for how it performs.
Own training and standards. Set what people are trained on, qualified in, and expected to keep current, then verify it is happening and hold the records that prove it. Build a team that deploys on short notice and stays that way.
Own vendor and supplier management. Decide what we need and from whom, run competitive procurement, and set approval thresholds. Where a supplier is part of how we protect someone, they meet our standard.
Own incident response. Be the escalation point for protective events within your authority and make real-time calls on protection and resourcing. Escalate immediately on legal exposure, law enforcement involvement, or risk that reaches other teams, and write down what was decided and why.
Lead converged physical-cyber protection. Work with Protective Intelligence and Cyber Protective Services to read threat indicators and judge what testing and assessment findings actually mean. When a threat starts online, you decide how protection answers it.
Earn trust and keep friction low. Build relationships with the people we protect, their families, and their teams to make protection something they rely on rather than tolerate. Design the friction out, so we ask less of them for the same result.
We are excited about you because you bring…
Leadership and operating experience. Ten or more years in protective, security, or military operations, including five or more years managing people with hands-on responsibility for protective operations. You have held real decision authority, not advised someone who held it, and you are still close enough to the work to run it yourself.
Judgment under pressure. You make sound calls with incomplete information in fast-moving, high-consequence situations, and the record of those decisions holds up under later review.
Building, not inheriting. A track record of building or scaling protective capability and setting the standards, qualifications, and procedures other leads work to.
Breadth of scope. Experience running more than one protective discipline or program at the same time, including through other leads, accountable for cost, method, and staffing across all of it.
Technical fluency across physical and cyber security. You do not need to be a security engineer, but you need to think like one. You understand how networked systems are put together and how someone would go about taking them apart, you are comfortable with network security concepts, access control, surveillance, and residential security technology at the operational level, and you can tell whether a proposed fix actually closes the gap it claims to.
Service orientation and discretion. You have earned the confidence of the people you protect and the people close to them, and you have kept it. You handle sensitive information about who is protected, how, and where without exception.
Working well across teams. A record of partnering with intelligence, cybersecurity, legal, and business teams on matters that go beyond your authority.
Availability. Willingness to travel around 35 percent, with peaks near 50 percent, often on short notice, and to pick up the phone on protective events and serious escalations outside working hours.
Physical readiness for the work. The ability to stay on your feet and moving for long stretches across offices, residences, venues, and transit, to lift and carry equipment up to 50 pounds, to assist or move a person to safety, to work in tight spaces and sit in vehicles and aircraft for extended periods, to see and assess people, vehicles, and conditions at distance and in poor light, to communicate clearly in loud environments, and to drive in heavy traffic and bad conditions.
Endurance for the conditions. The ability to work outdoors and in transit in extreme heat, extreme cold, inclement weather, and crowds for as long as the work takes, to work irregular and long hours including nights, weekends, and holidays on short or broken sleep and across time zones, and to keep making good decisions while doing it.
Education. Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.

title: Senior Data Engineer
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
Senior Data Engineer - Schaumburg
MISUMI | Data Platform
Own the data platform that MISUMI runs on
MISUMI is looking for a Senior Data Engineer to be the go-to owner of our Snowflake warehouse, dbt project, and data pipelines. You will be the primary data engineer, with real ownership and real influence: the models you build and the pipelines you run are what Operations, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Product, and Customer Support rely on to make decisions every day.
You will work hands-on with a modern stack (Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran, Git/GitHub) and with AI coding agents in your daily engineering work. You will also have the autonomy to take requests from intake to production, propose what we should build next, and shape safe team practices for agentic development. If you want a role where your judgment directly determines whether the business can trust its data, this is it.
Impact in this Role
The Senior Data Engineer is the go-to owner of MISUMI’s Snowflake warehouse, dbt project, and data pipelines. This person turns data from business and production systems into trusted, analytics-ready models that Operations, Finance, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Product, and Customer Support use to make decisions. Because this is the primary data engineering role, the accuracy, security, and reliability of the data platform, including regulated data such as CUI, depend on this person’s judgment and execution.
Essential Functions
Administer Snowflake: manage users, roles, grants, warehouses, resource monitors and security policies, and keep the environment secure, fast and cost-efficient.
Design, build, and own dbt models (staging, intermediate, marts, and the semantic layer) that turn replicated source data into trusted, analytics-ready tables with tests and documentation.
Build, operate, and monitor ELT pipelines from production and business systems into Snowflake, using Fivetran and related tools. Resolve connector failures, schema changes, backfills, and data-quality issues.
Act as the team’s primary technical resource for modeling and pipeline work. Take requests from intake to production independently, including scoping, estimating, and reporting status.
Translate business requirements into technical requirements and data models, and bridge the gap between business teams and technology. Ask clarifying questions, agree on metric definitions and acceptance criteria with stakeholders, and turn them into specifications the team can build and test.
Proactively identify opportunities where data, modeling, or automation can help the business get closer to its goals, and propose and prioritize them with stakeholders instead of waiting for requests.
Run an impact analysis before changing, deprecating, or removing any shared table, model, or connector. Use dbt lineage, Snowflake dependency and access metadata, and stakeholder review, and document a rollback plan.
Own the Git and GitHub workflow for the dbt project: branching standards, pull-request review, automated tests, and deployment.
Use AI assistants and agentic workflows in daily engineering work to speed up SQL and dbt development, testing, documentation, code review, and debugging, and help set safe team practices for using them.
Find the root cause of data-quality, performance, and pipeline problems and fix them at the source.
Tune queries, models, and warehouse usage, and advise engineers and analysts on efficient query patterns and table design.
Maintain data dictionaries, data-flow diagrams, and schema documentation.
Lead data design sessions and technical reviews, and explain design trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Evaluate new Snowflake and dbt features and tools, and recommend improvements to the data platform.
Mentor analysts and engineers on SQL and dbt best practices.
Work with remote, cross-functional teams across time zones.
Maintain and contribute to the Quality Management System (QMS).
Desired Traits
Five core skills. Candidates must show direct, hands-on production experience in each:
Snowflake administration and engineering: access control, warehouse sizing and cost control, query tuning, clustering, security controls, cloning, time travel, and data sharing.
dbt expert modeling: layered models, dimensional modeling, incremental models, snapshots, macros, tests, documentation, and CI/CD through Git.
Advanced SQL: CTEs, window functions, recursive queries, semi-structured data, and query tuning.
ETL/ELT tooling: Fivetran (our tool) or similar, including connector setup, schema drift, deleted records, backfills, and cost.
Agentic coding and development: daily use of AI coding agents that work in the repository and terminal (not chat-only use), with disciplined verification of everything they produce.
Required
Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of experience as a data engineer, designing, building, and operating data pipelines and warehouses.
6+ years of hands-on Snowflake experience in production, including administration: access control, warehouse management, and cost and performance monitoring.
5+ years building and maintaining production dbt projects (dbt Core or dbt Cloud), including testing, documentation, incremental models, macros, and CI/CD.
5+ years working with ETL/ELT tools such as Fivetran, Airbyte, Stitch, Matillion, Informatica, or Talend, plus experience with pipeline orchestration.
Demonstrated, hands-on experience using agentic coding tools that work directly in the codebase (not chat-only AI use) in daily data engineering work. This includes building agentic workflows or tool integrations for data work, such as MCP servers, custom agents, or automated dbt and pipeline checks, with concrete examples of the workflows and results.
Expert SQL, including CTEs, window functions, and performance tuning.
Daily use of Git and GitHub pull-request workflows.
Experience being the primary or sole owner of a data platform, or the technical lead for one.
Experience administering data platforms that hold regulated data (such as CUI under NIST SP 800-171), including access control, audit logging, encryption, and data classification. Must be able to pass a background check and complete required CUI and security training.
Preferred
Direct Fivetran experience, including connector management.
Experience with Sigma Computing, or with Tableau, Looker, or a similar BI tool.
Experience modeling ERP and CRM data, such as NetSuite or Salesforce.
Python for data tooling and automation.
Snowflake SnowPro certification or dbt certification.
Infrastructure-as-code experience for Snowflake, such as Terraform.
Background in manufacturing, supply chain, or marketplace businesses.
Abilities
Write advanced SQL on large, complex datasets, including semi-structured data such as JSON in Snowflake VARIANT columns.
Apply data warehousing and dimensional modeling principles to turn business requirements into well-structured, maintainable models.
Work independently: take an open-ended problem, define the approach, deliver it, and raise risks early instead of stalling.
Use sound production judgment: verify before changing shared systems, plan for failure, and know how to roll back.
Use AI tools with discipline: give clear context and constraints, review and test every AI-generated change, and stay accountable for the result.
Solve hard problems methodically: break an unclear problem into testable hypotheses, gather evidence from logs, lineage, and query history, confirm the cause before changing anything, and verify the fix worked.
Communicate clearly in writing and in person, giving business context to engineers and technical context to non-engineers.
Physical Demands
The employee routinely sits, talks, hears, and uses hands and fingers to operate a keyboard. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Travel
Ability to travel 5% annually in the US for team meetings, offsites, and conferences.
Ready to own the platform?
If you have run production Snowflake, dbt, and ELT at scale, you work daily with agentic coding tools, and you want to be the person the business trusts with its data, we would like to hear from you. Apply today.
Salary range:
$167,000 - $202,300 base salary per year, depending on experience
Benefits include, but are not limited to:
Comprehensive medical and dental coverage
401(k) plan
Generous PTO and leave programs
We’re actively seeking teammates who:
Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.
Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates
We encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, members of the LGBTQ community, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans.

title: Electromechanical Technician
description:
Job Description:
SUMMARY
Performs all related duties necessary for maintenance and repair of machinery and equipment used in production plant; for maintenance and repair of the physical structure, electrical, and plumbing systems of the buildings; and, when necessary, performs various construction/remodeling duties to company property as assigned.  Also performs electrical maintenance and repairs of plant production equipment and commercial building.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Follows all company safety rules and policies.
Must be able to maintain 5S program standards including organizing, labeling, cleaning and sustaining of workstations, toolboxes, work areas and parts shelving and cabinets.
Must be able to read, understands and follows schematics, wire and parts diagrams, sketches, operation manuals and manufacturer’s specifications to repair and maintain machinery and mechanical equipment such as, but not limited to, motors, pneumatic, hydraulic, conveyor systems and production machines and equipment using hand tools, power tools and precision measuring and testing instruments.
Observes mechanical devices in operation and listens to their sounds to locate causes of trouble. Root Cause
Dismantles machines or equipment to gain access to and remove defective parts, replaces defective parts and motors, and adjusts feed mechanisms.  Replaces or repairs machine belts.  Performs these duties with the aid of such equipment as hoists, cranes, hand tools and power tools.
Holds scaffolding members in place or tightens bolts to erect working platforms about machines.
Cleans and lubricates machine parts, such as, but not limited to, shafts, pulleys, gears, and bearings, using rags, brushes, grease gun, oil can, and other required tools not specifically listed here.
Removes dust, dirt, grease and waste material from machines.
Painting machines or equipment to prevent corrosion.
May install and repair electrical systems and electrical and electronic components of industrial machinery and equipment, following electrical code, manuals, schematic diagrams, blueprints and other specifications, using hand tools, power tools and electrical and electronic test equipment.
Observes functioning of installed equipment or system to detect hazards and need for adjustments, relocation or replacement.
May diagnose/troubleshoot malfunctioning equipment, such as control circuits, motors and lighting fixtures, HVAC systems, using testing equipment, and make necessary repairs, such as replacing damaged or broken wires and cables. Troubleshoot to component levels
Tests malfunctioning machinery, using test equipment and discusses malfunction with other maintenance employees to diagnose malfunction.  Replaces faulty electrical components of machinery, such as wiring, fuses, relays, switches, electric motor bearings and motors and positions sensing devices.
May diagnose and repair or replace faulty electronic components, such as circuit boards, and mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic components of machines and equipment.
Maintains tools and equipment and keeps supplies and parts in order.
May repair electronic equipment such as industrial controls, audio systems, transmitters, and servomechanisms, following blueprints and manufacturers’ specifications and using hand tools and test instruments.
Converses with machinery/equipment operators to ascertain problems with machinery/equipment before breakdown and to determine if breakdown is due to human error or mechanical/electrical problems.
Tests faulty machinery/equipment and applies knowledge of functional operation of electronic/electrical systems or units to diagnose cause of malfunction.
Tests electronic components and circuits to locate defects, using oscilloscopes, signal generators, ammeters and voltmeters. Replaces defective components and wiring and adjusts mechanical parts, using hand tools and soldering iron.  Aligns, adjusts and calibrates equipment according to specifications.
Maintains records of repairs, calibrations and tests.
May connect wiring to lighting fixtures and power equipment, using hand tools.  May install control and distribution components such as switches, relays and circuit-breaker panels, fastening in place with screws or bolts, using hand tools and power tools.
May connect power cables to equipment and installs grounding leads.
Tests continuity of circuit to ensure electrical compatibility and safety of components using testing instruments, such as ohmmeter, battery and buzzer and oscilloscope.
May bend and cut conduit and wire, and drill holes in walls, floors and ceilings for electrical connections.
May connect wire to motors, fixtures, and other electrical equipment, replace switches and fuses and splice wire and insulates wire with friction tape.
May bend, cut and thread pipe, cut openings in walls, ceilings and floors for pipes, seal pipe joints with sealing compound.
May cut out and join parts for worktables, benches, shelves and other furnishings, using power tools and hand tools.
May be required to assist with plumbing repair work, building construction/remodeling/repairs, general machinery maintenance or repair duties.
May patch or replace plaster or plaster board and paint walls, ceilings, and trim of building.
May drill and break up concrete.
May mix and pour concrete for foundations.
May weld and fabricate a variety of deigns, including fixtures, carts, tables, and platforms using MIG, TIG and/or stick methods.
Clears clogged drains and replaces plumbing fixtures.
Inspects products and processes while performing job duties to ensure all work done meets or exceeds standards of the company’s quality program.
Works cooperatively and congenially with co-workers to achieve cohesive and productive work processes and work environment.
May provide ground watch for other maintenance employees using aerial equipment
May be required to assist with spill response clean-up
May be required to train other maintenance employees
Performs additional tasks as assigned by management or as the situation requires.
QUALIFICATIONS
Valid Texas Driver’s License required
3 + years’ experience in general mechanical maintenance of production machinery to include reading blueprints, wire diagrams, pneumatics, hydraulics, welding, root cause analysis, and requesting machine parts.
Possess minimum knowledge of electrical wiring repairs and installation, AC/DC controls, blueprints, schematic diagrams, pneumatics, and hydraulics.
Technical degree and/or license relating to electrical, mechanical or HVAC/Refrigeration - minimum of one preferred OR 40 hours of documented electrical training. License number and/or documentation must be provided before hire date.
Must be able to meet all minimum training requirements within first 6-12 months of hire date.
Obtain and Maintain Traulsen/OSHA certifications for powered equipment, including but not limited to, forklifts, scissor lifts, aerial booms, stock chasers, and floor scrubbers within first 90 days of hire date.
Capable of operating aerial lift equipment
Obtain and maintain Traulsen/OSHA certifications for power equipment.
Ability to follow verbal and written instructions regarding procedures required for various machine repair.
Ability to read and follow repair or installation instructions
Ability to use a variety of small hand tools, power tools, scissors lifts, and material handling equipment.
Possess basic mechanical aptitude and ability.
Ability to communicate clearly with co-workers (bi-lingual English-Spanish a plus)
Ability to read and follow written English instructions and complete PMs and work orders within Maintenance CMMS software. Some ability to write English responses.
Ability to understand basic online safety and cyber security courses presented in English and demonstrate understanding through multiple choice exam score
Ability to communicate through email
PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT
Attend work regularly and report promptly for duty on the days and at the times scheduled by the supervisor.
Schedule changes occur and should be handled in a productive manner
Working temperatures vary with seasonal changes where climate control is limited.  The environment is one in which noise exists.
Work occasionally outdoors in temperatures ranging from hot to cold and exposed to rain and wind
Sit on a forklift, stand, walk, squat, climb, or crawl for a combined minimum of eight (8) to ten (10) hours per day on a concrete surface.
Lift and carry components, tools, or other items weighing more than 35 pounds.  Any item over 35 pounds, is to be done with assistance
Pull and push up to 100 pounds.
Ability to work around hazardous chemicals.
Carries tools and equipment to and from storage and work areas.
May perform combination of physical movements to reach areas difficult to access including bending, stooping, squatting, reaching, twisting and rotation motions using head/neck, arms, wrists, waist, knees and arms while performing duties.
Handle small hand tools and power tools.  Handling may be done unilaterally (one-handed) or bilaterally (two-handed) depending on size and shape of object and task being performed.
Need corrected vision to be aware of surroundings and location of items needed and perform various other job duties.
Need corrected hearing to identify conditions in the environment (i.e. forklift horns, fire alarms).
Need mental alertness to identify, avoid, or resolve safety hazards.
Ability to work at elevated heights.
Ability to communicate with supervisors and co-workers.
Ability to wear designated personal protective equipment for the work assignment (i.e. safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, hearing protection, harnesses, hard hats, safety shoes)
Hours of Work

description:
Job Description:
Smart People. Smart Ideas. Smart Choice.
Hands-On Field Service Role
MTS is a leading global supplier of test and simulation systems. Formula 1 teams, leading automotive and aerospace companies, and the world's top researchers in materials and seismic engineering all rely on our systems to determine product reliability and ensure compliance with quality standards. Check out some of our amazing technology here: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vXOsvWpTHH4
What This Role Looks Like
This is a unique, HQ-based Field Service Engineer role for someone who thrives on variety over a fixed territory. As our floater FSE based in Eden Prairie, MN, you'll step into a trainer's or mentor's territory anywhere in North America for the full duration of each training or mentoring event, keeping coverage seamless while they're out. When no event is active, you'll cover PTO, illness, and peak overflow. Being based at MTS headquarters means faster ramp-up, direct access to SMEs and training resources, and central dispatch to wherever coverage is needed next.
Day to day, the work is hands-on: installing, maintaining, calibrating, and troubleshooting complex servo-hydraulic and electro-mechanical test systems at customer sites. Training on MTS-specific technology is provided, and strong hands-on technical aptitude is essential.
Travel: This role involves frequent travel from home base in Eden Prairie, MN to customer sites across North America, since coverage assignments follow wherever a training or mentoring event or overflow need arises. Travel will vary week to week rather than following a fixed regional pattern, and candidates should be genuinely comfortable with, and energized by, a highly travel-oriented role.
Key Responsibilities
Install, maintain, calibrate, and repair computer-controlled servo-hydraulic and electro-mechanical test systems
Diagnosing issues across controllers, hydraulics, data acquisition systems, sensors, transducers, fixtures, and grips
Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and control-system issues using hands-on diagnostic methods
Perform calibrations independently for assigned customer systems

description:
Job Description:
ITW Food Equipment Group LLC designs and manufactures commercial food equipment for food service and retail customers through its subsidiaries. The company’s products include ware washing equipment; cooking equipment, including ovens, ranges, and broilers; refrigeration equipment, including refrigerators, freezers, and prep tables; food processing equipment, including slicers, mixers, and scales; and kitchen exhaust, ventilation, and pollution control systems. The company was incorporated in 2001 and is based in Troy, Ohio. ITW Food Equipment Group LLC is an Illinois Tool Works Inc. subsidiary.
SUMMARY
This position is responsible for providing comprehensive administrative and operational support within an assigned territory. The role focuses on work order approval, invoicing, billing discrepancies, and daily invoice printing. The Operational Support Administrator will also adhere to the service territory backup structure and manage various accounts receivable tasks. The company has manufacturing locations in Pennsylvania, California, Hungary, Malaysia and Korea, and also maintains sales and service offices throughout the world. Our high-tech products are used in laboratory and process applications in end markets such as: oil & gas, petrochemical, medical devices, waste water, life sciences, and analytical instruments.
Brooks is a division of ITW (Illinois Tool Works), a fortune 200 company. ITW is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. The company has operations in 56 countries and employs over 50,000 employees. These talented employees, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to ITW’s global leadership in innovation. The company is proud of its broad portfolio of nearly 10,000 active patents, and is focused on fully leveraging its highly differentiated business model to deliver solid growth with consistent best-in-class margins and return on capital.
Basic Function
The 1st shift Production Supervisor provides direct leadership and operational oversight for first- and second-shift employees manufacturing Industrial products at the Brooks Instrument facility in Hatfield, Pennsylvania. Working a schedule designed to provide meaningful coverage and visibility across both shifts, the supervisor ensures consistent execution of safety, quality, delivery, productivity, inventory, cost, housekeeping, and employee-performance expectations.
The supervisor serves as the primary connection between the two shifts, maintaining clear priorities, effective handoffs, and consistent application of policies and operating practices. This role works closely with the Production Operations Manager, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Materials, Supply Chain, Human Resources, and other partners to resolve issues, develop employees, meet customer requirements, and drive continuous improvement through the ITW Toolbox and Lean Manufacturing methods.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
•       Provide direct supervision, daily direction, coaching, and performance management for assigned first- and second-shift employees supporting Industrial production.
•       Maintain a regular work schedule that overlaps first and second shifts sufficiently to provide leadership visibility, employee access, direct observation, communication, and accountability across both shifts.
•       Establish and communicate daily production priorities, staffing assignments, schedules, output requirements, and operational expectations based on customer demand and business needs.
•       Coordinate effective handoffs between first and second shifts, including status of production, staffing, materials, equipment, quality issues, safety concerns, and open actions.
•       Ensure production plans, procedures, quality requirements, and performance expectations are applied consistently across both shifts.
•       Create and maintain a healthy and safe work environment; ensure employees understand and follow all safety requirements, personal protective equipment rules, cleanroom or gowning procedures, and incident-reporting expectations.
•       Lead daily management and gemba activities; review results against plan, identify gaps, assign corrective actions, remove obstacles, and ensure timely follow-through.
•       Monitor, analyze, and communicate key performance indicators, including safety, quality, output, on-time delivery, productivity, labor efficiency, yield, scrap, rework, cycle time, overtime, inventory accuracy, and attendance.
•       Organize work, allocate available labor, and adjust priorities throughout the day to address changing demand, staffing constraints, material availability, equipment issues, and production interruptions.
•       Maintain thorough working knowledge of assigned Vacuum and Pressure products, manufacturing processes, equipment, work cells, documentation, and operating requirements.
•       Partner with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality to troubleshoot production issues, identify root causes, implement corrective actions, and sustain approved process or product changes.
•       Coordinate with Materials and Supply Chain to address component shortages, inventory discrepancies, work-in-process concerns, and other constraints affecting the production schedule.
•       Ensure employees accurately complete required production, inventory, quality, training, timekeeping, and other business-system transactions and documentation.
•       Promote 5S, visual management, standard work, flow, mistake-proofing, waste reduction, and other ITW Toolbox and Lean Manufacturing practices throughout assigned production areas.
•       Evaluate production operations, workflows, staffing, and methods to identify opportunities to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, and employee effectiveness.
•       Ensure assigned employees are appropriately trained and qualified; maintain training plans and records and provide cross-training to build flexibility and coverage across both shifts.
•       Provide ongoing feedback, conduct performance discussions and reviews, recognize strong performance, and address attendance, conduct, or performance concerns in partnership with Human Resources.
•       Support employee hiring, interviewing, selection, onboarding, training, engagement, development, and retention activities.
•       Coach, mentor, and develop employees and emerging leaders; identify development opportunities and support succession planning for critical production roles.
•       Communicate company information, policy changes, production updates, and business priorities accurately and consistently to employees on both shifts.
•       Ensure established company policies, work rules, procedures, quality standards, and regulatory requirements are communicated, understood, and followed.
•       Collaborate with other supervisors and functional partners to coordinate shared resources, resolve cross-functional problems, and support overall site and customer priorities.
•       Support customer complaint investigations, corrective actions, audits, and other quality-system activities as assigned.
•       Prepare and communicate production, staffing, overtime, attendance, quality, delivery, and operational updates to the Production Operations Manager and other stakeholders.
•       Promote a respectful, inclusive, accountable, and team-oriented work environment across both shifts.
•       Support company continuous improvement initiatives and perform other duties as assigned. Marginal functions not listed among the essential duties may also be required.
Education and Experience
•       Bachelor's degree in engineering, technology, operations management, business administration, or a related field preferred.
•       Minimum of three years of supervisory or team-leadership experience in a manufacturing or production environment required.
•       Experience supervising employees across multiple shifts or working a split-shift schedule strongly preferred.
•       Experience with vacuum, pressure, flow-control, instrumentation, semiconductor, electromechanical, or other complex technical products preferred.
•       Demonstrated experience implementing Lean Manufacturing, daily management, 5S, visual management, standard work, or other continuous improvement methods preferred.
•       Experience working within an ISO 9001 or similarly regulated quality-system environment preferred
Knowledge Skills and Abilities
•       Proven ability to lead, motivate, coach, and hold employees accountable while maintaining positive working relationships.
•       Strong knowledge of manufacturing operations, production scheduling, labor allocation, inventory processes, quality requirements, and performance metrics.
•       Ability to maintain consistent communication, expectations, and follow-through across first- and second-shift teams.
•       Strong decision-making and problem-solving skills, including the ability to assess priorities and respond effectively to production disruptions or escalations.
•       Excellent verbal and written communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with employees, peers, managers, and cross-functional partners.
•       Strong organizational, time-management, documentation, and follow-through skills.
•       Ability to handle confidential employee and business information with discretion and sound judgment.
•       Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint; experience with ERP, manufacturing execution, quality, timekeeping, or data-reporting systems preferred.
•       Ability to work onsite in Hatfield on a split-shift schedule and adjust working hours periodically to support operational needs, employee meetings, training, or critical issues.

Health and dental insurance
Company Paid Life Insurance
Short and Long Term Disability
401K plan with generous company match
Vacation, personal days and holidays
Continuing education reimbursement program

title: Strategic Sourcing Intern - Summer 2027
description:

Since its founding more than 100 years ago, ITW has become one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. We place a high premium on the development of innovative solutions–most of which are developed in tandem with our customers. And we continue to ensure that our customers receive timely, cost-effective service for the innovative products we provide.
ITW’s differentiated business model is composed of a set of unique core capabilities: our proprietary 80/20 business process, customer-back innovation, and our well-known decentralized entrepreneurial culture. These capabilities are unmistakably ITW—and key to our longevity and strong performance.
ITW’s products and solutions are at work all over the world, in deep-sea oil rigs, aerospace technology, bridges and wind turbines, healthcare, the spaces in which we live and work, the cars we drive, and the mobile devices we rely on. We are seeking an experienced Senior BI Analyst to support the design and delivery of Finance reporting, analytics, data products, and process-improvement solutions. Working closely with the Finance Product Owner, this role will serve as an onsite analytical partner to Finance stakeholders and a key link between business, application, data engineering, and reporting teams.

Technical Translation & Requirements Gathering: Partner with the Finance Product Owner and Finance stakeholders to understand business processes, controls, and reporting needs. BI Design & Solution Delivery: Design, build, and maintain Finance dashboards, published data sources, BI data models, operational reports, and self-service analytics solutions using Tableau, Power BI, or comparable platforms.
Lineage, Reconciliation & Root-Cause Analysis: Analyze end-to-end processes and data flows across ERP (SAP), CRM, billing, data warehouse, and reporting platforms. Use advanced SQL and analytical tools to reconcile data, validate business rules, investigate discrepancies, and identify root causes.
Performance Tuning & Reporting Reliability: Optimize dashboard usability, query performance, data refresh schedules, metric consistency, and overall reporting reliability.
Delivery Leadership & Governance : Lead assigned workstreams through requirements, solution design, UAT, regression testing, reconciliation, implementation readiness, and stakeholder sign-off. Maintain data definitions, reporting specifications, test evidence, user guides, and governance documentation.
Internal Controls & Quality Monitoring: Support automated monitoring, exception management, data-quality controls, and financially significant/SOX-governed reporting processes.
Cross-Functional & Global Collaboration: Collaborate with application, Data Engineering, Data Science, AI, and platform teams while coordinating and reviewing deliverables across distributed onsite and offshore resources.
Applied AI & Automation Evaluation: Evaluate and support opportunities to implement intelligent alerts, natural-language analytics, AI-assisted analysis, and workflow automation within core Finance processes.
Qualifications
Required Skills and Experience
7+ years of progressive experience in business intelligence, Finance analytics, reporting, business systems analysis, or enterprise data solutions.
ERP & Finance Domain: Experience with SAP or another enterprise ERP platform, including strong understanding of Finance-related processes and cross-system data flows.
Advanced SQL Mastery: Expert-level SQL skills for complex querying, source-to-target reconciliation, data troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and query performance optimization.
Enterprise BI Platforms: Strong hands-on experience designing dashboards, BI data models, calculated metrics, published data sources, and self-service solutions in Tableau , Power BI , or a comparable enterprise analytics platform.
Data Architecture Fundamentals: Solid understanding of data warehousing concepts, dimensional modeling, semantic layers, data quality, lineage, and visualization best practices.
Delivery & Testing Leadership: Demonstrated experience translating business needs into technical specifications and leading UAT, regression testing, issue resolution, and business-readiness activities.
Communication & Influence: Proven ability to communicate complex business, system, and data topics to technical teams, Finance stakeholders, and senior leadership without direct authority.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with SAP Finance, Salesforce, CPQ/CLM, billing, or revenue-management platforms.
Experience with Snowflake or another modern cloud data platform.
Experience supporting financially significant applications, internal controls, or SOX-governed reporting.
Familiarity with data governance, master data management (MDM), metadata, lineage, and data-quality frameworks.
Exposure to AI-assisted analytics, natural-language querying, intelligent monitoring, Snowflake Cortex, or comparable emerging technologies.
Experience coordinating and reviewing work with distributed onsite and offshore analysts or consultants.
Required Education
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Systems, Business Analytics, Finance, Accounting, Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a related field.
What Success Looks Like
Develops a strong understanding of Finance processes, ERP applications, system integrations, critical data models, and reporting dependencies.
Establishes effective translation and validation practices between Finance stakeholders and technical delivery teams, serving as a trusted onsite partner.
Delivers accurate, intuitive, and performant dashboards and BI solutions that stakeholders trust for day-to-day decision-making and operational reviews.
Independently uses SQL and analytical tools to reconcile data across systems, trace transformations, validate business rules, and identify root causes.
Improves reporting reliability and governance , expanding exception monitoring, data-quality controls, metric consistency, and self-service analytics adoption.
Helps Finance teams adopt automation and AI-assisted analytics where they provide measurable business value and practical process improvements.

This position is seeking a creative and flexible individual to help lead the Planning activities for the Instrument or Systems Manufacturing lines. Responsible for the overall status of order fulfillment and managing inventory levels throughout the manufacturing process.
The Sr Production Planner will be assigned critical Operations, NPI or Sustaining projects to manage.  Expected to seek out and recommend process improvements, assist in developing team members skill sets in the planning, take on leadership responsibilities for strategic planning activities that enable the department capabilities to scale to the growing business needs.
The candidate will work with multiple cross-functional teams, Manufacturing, Supply chain, Quality, Engineering and other teams to achieve both tactical and strategic goals assigned.  This by fully understanding production demand and supply needs, balancing operational goals while incorporating Lean Manufacturing principals, and identify and coordinate issue resolution and continuous improvement opportunities with other departments. This position requires strong presentation and clear communication abilities.
Essential Job Duties
·         Manage assigned NPI/Sustaining projects at both strategic and tactical level. Evaluate current process and recommend continuous improvement to evolve process.
·         Provides mentorship through tactical training to team members to improve their skill sets in NPI/ Sustaining planning. Lead efforts to create and/or updating work instructions (WI) & Departmental Operating Procedures (DOP).
·         Lead and support department or organizational projects. Gain project team consensus, track/ monitor scope, scope changes, project plan time lines against phase review objectives, variances and contingencies that surface during implementation of projects. Escalate where necessary to management.
·         Engage Manufacturing teams in the continuous improvement process to ensure assigned projects are identified, prioritized and implemented in a timely and effective manner.
·         Identify potential supply risks and inventory exposures by aligning supply chain processes with production plan milestones/targets. Illuminate impact to supply continuity for Finished Goods Inventory (FGI).
·         Applying knowledge of concepts and principles of planning to develop solutions to a variety of problems, particularly with supply constraints.
·         Perform capacity analysis in to support what-if scenarios, forecast changes, and plan for production growth.
·         Maintain department metrics; analyze trends and results. Drive appropriate corrective actions where needed.
·         Provide direction to various NPI programs/projects as subject matter expert, to support product transitions to sustaining manufacturing lines.
·         Collaborate with Purchasing and Engineering to review proposed changes and establish Engineering Change Order (ECO) affectivity.  Execute ECO implementation requirements.
·         Support production activities and ensure maximum line up-time
·         Determine and manage potential line shortages by analyzing build schedules, shortage reports, on hand inventory reports and supplier delivery information
·         Develop communication relationship with Production, Engineering, Purchasing, Shipping, and Customer Service to manage supply and demand
·         Resolve work order variances, and determine/track root cause. Work with Cost Accounting for month end close
·         Monitor and adjust planning parameters in SAP

Minimum 2 years’ experience in SAP.(Mandatory)
Advanced MS Office skills, understanding of vlookup, Pivot tables, macro recordings, data tables, charting, data sorting segregation and formula auditing.
Presents ideas effectively in formal and informal situations. Conveys thoughts clearly and concisely.
Ability to respond to detailed inquiries, and present information to groups and senior management.
Advanced SAP/ERP experience, troubleshoot IT issues that surface with little to no assistance from business applications. Lead department customization transaction Tcode enhancements for business needs.

Expert knowledge of business disciplines production planning and supply chain management.
Ability to perform with greater independence and judgment, receiving general supervision from senior management.

Exposure to low volume, high complexity capital equipment or high volume, low complexity products.
Highly analytical: critical-thinker; strong analytical aptitude and attention to detail; due to the speed and rate of change occurring in this manufacturing environment, must be able to problem solve and think independently.
Flexible: adaptable and able to work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.
Motivated: enthusiastic; strives for excellence; continually seeks to improve self and company; ability and strong desire to grow with the company; leads by example.
Ability to handle multiple tasks and projects successfully.
Required Education and Training
·         Minimum 5  years of experience in a progressive manufacturing environment, 4 year degree preferred in Business Management or Engineering .
Preferred Skills and Experience
APICS certification a plus.
Preferred experience in the Pharmaceutical or Medical Device industry (or similar regulated industry). Demonstrate the ability to operate in a regulated industry with working knowledge of ISO and regulatory restrictions.

Design and develop product-focused, robust and efficient robotics system software (C/C++) and software for observability applications (auto issue detection, log replay), pipelines and analytics to help understand system software status (events, logs, data streams), construct system event timeline and analyze complex multimodal robotics system issues.
Design and develop robust applications (Python) to analyze system status from Logs, Events and Data streams (either locally interfacing to system or from backend)
Identify and prove out new architectural enhancements to the software infrastructure and development processes that elevate the broader organization beyond your own team.
Contribute to multiple areas of software development, including but not limited to the following: Design and development of robotic system software.
Robotics system introspection, observability, and system event timeline visualization of Intuitive’s robotic surgical platform.
Real-time processing performance analysis.
Extension of current processing frameworks to next generations of products.
Bring-up of research prototypes used to evaluate new product concepts.
Design and development of hardware / software diagnostic tools.
Unit testing and code integration efforts to ensure exceptional system reliability and robustness.
Contribute to conducting system failure analysis, identifying issues, risks, and discussing effective mitigation strategies.
Interface and collaborate with multiple teams, including Embedded System Software, User Interface Software Engineering, Data pipeline & analytics, Field Service User Applications, System Test and reliability Engineering to bring robotics observability applications from prototype to launch
Document software designs according to Intuitive's development and quality guidelines.

Minimum of 8 years of experience and a Bachelor's degree; or 6 years of experience and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years of experience; or equivalent experience
Proficiency in C/C++ and experience with Python
Familiarity building embedded software and/or distributed systems and/or applications that operate on observability data (log, events, data streams) from robotics or embedded devices
Preferred Skills & Experience
Experience working with robotics and system software for complex distributed systems
Comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis
Demonstrated experience and comfort with all phases of the product development lifecycle (design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing)
Experience or familiarity working with data platform teams and developing data pipelines for embedded devices data
Familiarity with applications for system observability, processing, visualization and automatic issue detection for robotics systems (analysis using python in cloud based on system events, logs, data – applying known signatures or ML based techniques)
Experience with data visualization and knowledgeable in full stack software development
Familiarity with deployment infrastructure along with CI/CD pipelines

The primary responsibility of the position is to lead the software team responsible for implementing the User Interface and underlying State Machine of the SP system. The UI Manager works collaboratively with a cross-functional team of interaction designers, human factors engineers, clinical engineers, and others to develop embedded software and graphical user interfaces that make customers’ experience of using complex surgical devices safe, easy to learn, and confidence-inspiring.  The successful candidate is a hands-on technical manager able to drive to solutions from rough requirements and has a commitment to high product quality. A strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward is required.
Essential Job Duties
Recognize and attract top talent, mentor and train existing team members and new hires through one-on-one coaching as well as team wide initiatives.
Interface with variety of cross functional teams including Interaction Design, Human Factors, Clinical, Controls Engineering, etc., in understanding user interface needs to create, maintain, and track a bottom-up schedule that best supports business unit top-down goals.
Own full development lifecycle for UI software team and associated documentation (negotiate requirements, systematic risk assessment and mitigation, prototyping, development, testing, and software releases).
Champion best practices in software development (code reviews, scrums, bug scrubbing meetings, coding conventions, continuous integration, defensive programming, static analysis, design patterns, etc.).
Conduct technical design reviews.
Assess and update the software hazard analysis and identify mitigations for hazardous situations.
Document traceability from software requirements and software hazard analyses to module verification tests and system verification tests.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience recruiting, mentoring, and functionally managing teams of highly skilled engineers.
Experience in all phases of software development including evaluation, planning and definition, design & implementation, Verification & Validation, Market Launch, and Post Market.
Experience with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.
Hands-on engineering experience developing User Interface software.
Excellent teamwork skills with proven ability to collaborate across multiple teams.
Excellent communication and documentation skills.
High attention to detail.
Strong people management abilities with ability to ensure team success.
Ability to build and maintain relationships across organizations.
Experience with revision control systems (e.g. SVN and Git).
Experience with issue tracking software (e.g, JIRA)
Required Education and Training
Bachelor/Master/PhD degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Engineering or equivalent work experience.
10+ years industry experience developing and supporting embedded systems.
3+ years industry experience managing a team of User Interface software engineers.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with designing software products in an FDA or other regulated industry or for mission critical applications.
Experience with UI design.
Experience with QNX, QML, and Qt.
Experience with UML State machines.
Experience with Matlab, Python, or other scripting languages.
Experience with build systems such as GNU Make and CMake, EMake.

description:

About the Team
The Future Forward organization is Intuitive's advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery. Our research team is building advanced augmented dexterity capabilities for next-generation robotic platforms.
The Role
Our researchers should spend their time on ideas, not on the manual work required to turn those ideas into results on real robots.
As a Senior AI & Automation Engineer, you will build the AI tools, automation systems, integrations, and evaluation capabilities that help researchers and engineers train, test, and evaluate models faster and make better decisions. You'll leverage existing AI technologies while developing new solutions, from agent-driven workflows and AI tooling to the APIs, services, and automation frameworks that support engineering and research activities.
That could mean agents that set up and run experiments, automation workflows that accelerate testing and evaluation, or tools that sort through logs and video to help teams understand failures and improve outcomes. It's a hands-on engineering role that uses AI to improve how physical AI systems are trained and tested. You'll automate that work; you won't design the models themselves. You'll work closely with ML researchers, simulation engineers, and robotics engineers.
What You'll Do
• Build and integrate AI tools, APIs, and agent workflows that automate engineering and research work across the team.
• Automate the training and fine-tuning workflow, from setting up experiments to launching, tracking, and comparing runs, so researchers can reproduce results without hand-built scripts.
• Build automation and integration workflows that help researchers and engineers evaluate new ideas in simulation and on real robots, quickly, reliably, and at scale.
• Design evaluations and experiments that show, with statistical confidence, whether a change is a real improvement.
• Build logging, analysis, and debugging tools that help the team understand results and failures, and that turn robot sessions into data the team can train on.
• Make what you build reliable, secure, and safe to run, with human approval where it matters and responsible use of AI throughout.
• Evaluate emerging AI tools, models, and technologies, and bring in the ones that deliver measurable impact.
• Measure the impact of what you build, document it clearly, and make successful tools part of how the team operates.
What You Bring
We care more about real depth in a few of these areas than shallow coverage of all of them.
• Hands-on work with real robots. You've built testing, automation, or evaluation systems that ran on real robot hardware or other physical systems via software interfaces, not only in the cloud or in simulation.
• AI and automation you've built and put into daily use. You've built LLM-agent workflows, AI tool integrations, copilots, or automation pipelines for real engineering work and measured whether they helped. Be ready to walk us through one: what it did, where it failed, and what you changed.
• Evaluation and experimental rigor. You know how to design experiments and understand the statistics needed to determine whether an improvement is real.
• Strong software engineering. You have 5+ years of software engineering experience.
You write production-quality Python, can read C++, and are comfortable with Linux, CI/CD, Docker, containerized services, APIs, and distributed systems.
Strong candidates often come from robotics, autonomous systems, physical AI, or robot- learning research, and have applied AI tooling to real hardware. You're comfortable working across disciplines in a fast-moving research environment and can explain trade-offs clearly to researchers and engineers alike.
If you don't check every box, we still want to hear from you.
Education
• BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical
Engineering, or a related technical field.
• Advanced degree (MS or PhD) preferred.
Bonus Points
None of these are required. They're signals, not gates, and any one of them is a nice plus.
• Robotics simulation, such as NVIDIA Isaac Sim/Lab or MuJoCo
• Evaluating AI/ML, robotics, or robot-learning systems
• Surgical or medical robotics, including da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) systems
• ROS 2 or other robot middleware
• Agent frameworks, tool integrations, or MCP servers adopted by engineering teams
• AI assistants, copilots, or productivity tools built for engineers or researchers
• AI applied to scientific, engineering, or research workflows

title: Staff Mechanical Engineer - Future Opportunity
description:
At Intuitive, we are united behind our mission: we believe that minimally invasive care is life-enhancing care. Through ingenuity and intelligent technology, we expand the potential of physicians to heal without constraints.
As a pioneer and market leader in robotic-assisted surgery, we strive to foster an inclusive and diverse team, committed to making a difference. For more than 25 years, we have worked with hospitals and care teams around the world to help solve some of healthcare's hardest challenges and advance what is possible.
Intuitive has been built by the efforts of great people from diverse backgrounds. We believe great ideas can come from anywhere. We strive to foster an inclusive culture built around diversity of thought and mutual respect. We lead with inclusion and empower our team members to do their best work as their most authentic selves.
Passionate people who want to make a difference drive our culture. Our team members are grounded in integrity, have a strong capacity to learn, the energy to get things done, and bring diverse, real world experiences to help us think in new ways. We actively invest in our team members to support their long-term growth so they can continue to advance our mission and achieve their highest potential.
Join a team committed to taking big leaps forward for a global community of healthcare professionals and their patients. Together, let's advance the world of minimally invasive care.
The Staff Mechanical Design Engineer independently owns technically demanding mechanical and electromechanical subsystems for robotic systems. You will lead subsystem architecture and detailed-design decisions, resolve complex multidisciplinary problems, and contribute to integration decisions beyond your assigned subsystem.
This is a hands-on individual contributor role combining mechanical design ownership with technical guidance and mentorship. The role reports to a Manager of Mechanical Design Engineering in New Product Development.
Essential Job Duties
Own subsystem development from concept through verification and design transfer, including mechanical requirements, specifications, design-risk analyses and verification documentation. Support validation activities with the responsible functions.
Lead subsystem architecture decisions. Compare alternatives and justify tradeoffs.
Design precision mechanisms, joints and actuation assemblies. Select and size components such as motors, bearings, transmissions, brakes and sensors based on operating loads, motion requirements and expected life.
Use first-principles calculations and simulation to establish load paths, component margins, structural stiffness, dynamic behavior and fatigue life. Check assumptions and correlate models with test results.
Create and release CAD models, manufacturing drawings and design documentation. Apply GD&T and tolerance analysis to functional interfaces, assembly requirements and inspection.
Build, test, debug and iterate prototypes. Develop test methods and fixtures, investigate failures, and verify corrective actions.
Work directly with suppliers, supplier engineering, sourcing and manufacturing to resolve technical issues, improve DFM/DFA and cost, and prepare designs for transfer.
Collaborate with systems, electrical, controls, clinical, human factors, manufacturing, supplier engineering/sourcing, quality and regulatory partners to resolve requirements and subsystem interfaces.
Lead technical reviews and guide other engineers’ design and analysis approaches. Plan technical work across functions, set priorities, resolve risks and mentor engineers through problem-solving.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience developing robotic or complex electromechanical products in a regulated industry, with demonstrated independent subsystem ownership from concept through design transfer.
Working knowledge of design controls, risk management, verification and validation.
Deep expertise in first-principles mechanics and precision mechanisms, with demonstrated ability to perform stiffness, dynamics and fatigue analysis.
Proficiency in GD&T, tolerancing, materials, DFM/DFA and manufacturing processes.
Experience designing rotary or linear joints, sizing components, and justifying decisions through analysis; integrating actuation and sensing; and collaborating effectively with controls and electrical engineers.
Hands-on prototyping experience, including assembly, testing, debugging, and rapid iterations.
Proficient with CAD, simulation, and PLM tools such as SolidWorks, ANSYS, and Windchill.
Demonstrated technical leadership through design reviews, cross-functional decision-making, stakeholder influence and engineer mentorship.
Experience with risk management activities including FMEA, risk mitigation, and reliability assessments.
Required Education and Training
Required: Typical minimum Bachelor’s degree plus 12 years of relevant experience, or a Master’s degree plus 8 years, or a PhD plus 5 years.
Preferred: Master’s or PhD degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.
Working Conditions
On-site four days per week in Sunnyvale, CA.
May involve extended periods of computer-based design and analysis work.
Must be comfortable occasionally working in lab environments, including prototype assembly, mechanical testing, and safe use of standard mechanical tools and fixtures.
Must be able to occasionally lift and handle 25 pounds.

You will transform sourcing, supplier, inventory, and plant maintenance data into actionable insights that improve cost, working capital, supplier performance, contract compliance as well as increase our speed of decision making and sourcing execution.
You will partner with Category Buyers, Category Managers, Maintenance Leaders, Plant Stakeholders, Finance Stakeholders, Master Data Management team, IT, and suppliers to identify value opportunities, build repeatable analytical tools, quantify and validate savings, and strengthen the foundational data required to execute the MRO category strategy. Develop and maintain spend analytics across MRO categories, suppliers, plants, materials, and buying channels (SAP, Ariba catalog and non-catalog).
Clean, enrich, classify, and reconcile purchasing data, supplier invoices, catalog, contract, inventory, and material master data.
